+++ b/tools/cycle-ratio.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,158 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the two release-notes lines of a cycle, task-kind
+# counts and the volume ratio (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).
+#
+#   kinds: mechanical N · judgment N · operator N
+#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>
+#
+# Mapping (the glossary's "Kind counts" and "Volume ratio" entries):
+#   kinds          the 'kind: <value>' token that ends each top-level '- [ ]' /
+#                  '- [x]' task line under '### Technical Tasks', and each
+#                  '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside
+#                  a '## Sprint N' block of the sprint plan (fenced code skipped,
+#                  the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces);
+#                  untagged task lines are counted in --json and WARNed
+#   script lines   added + deleted lines of *.sh *.py *.ts *.js files between
+#                  the two commits (git diff --numstat, renames detected,
+#                  binary files skipped)
+#   prose bytes    bytes of the added and removed *.md lines between the two
+#                  commits, newline included, diff markers excluded
+#   model calls    MODELINV rows (primitive_id MODELINV) in the MODELINV log
+#                  whose ts_utc lies between the two commits' committer
+#                  timestamps, both ends included. The log is host-local, so
+#                  the count covers only the calls made on this host: "scope:
+#                  host". A missing log prints "model calls n/a" and a WARN.
+#
+# Git runs in the current directory's repository; --sprint-plan and --modelinv
+# default to paths under its top level.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tools/cycle-ratio.sh --from SHA --to SHA [--sprint-plan PATH]
+#                        [--modelinv PATH] [--json]
+#
+#   --sprint-plan PATH  default grimoires/loa/sprint.md
+#   --modelinv PATH     default .run/model-invoke.jsonl
+#   --json              one JSON object instead of the two lines
+#
+# Exit 2 also covers: not a git repository, an unreadable sprint plan, jq missing.
+# Exit codes: 0 printed · 2 usage or unreadable input · 3 a SHA names no commit
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+die() { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $2" >&2; exit "$1"; }
+
+SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+FENCE_AWK="$SCRIPT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/md-fence.awk"
+
+FROM=""
+TO=""
+PLAN=""
+MODELINV=""
+JSON=0
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --from|--to|--sprint-plan|--modelinv)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $1 needs a value" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
+      case "$1" in
+        --from) FROM="$2" ;;
+        --to) TO="$2" ;;
+        --sprint-plan) PLAN="$2" ;;
+        --modelinv) MODELINV="$2" ;;
+      esac
+      shift 2 ;;
+    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
+    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "cycle-ratio.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+[[ -n "$FROM" && -n "$TO" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: --from and --to are required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 2 "jq is required"
+TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die 2 "not inside a git repository"
+[[ -n "$PLAN" ]] || PLAN="$TOP/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
+[[ -n "$MODELINV" ]] || MODELINV="$TOP/.run/model-invoke.jsonl"
+[[ -r "$PLAN" && -f "$PLAN" ]] || die 2 "sprint plan not readable: $PLAN"
+[[ -r "$FENCE_AWK" ]] || die 2 "cannot read $FENCE_AWK (reinstall the framework scripts)"
+
+# A leading '-' would reach git as an option; a SHA never starts with one.
+case "$FROM" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM" ;; esac
+case "$TO" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $TO" ;; esac
+FROM_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${FROM}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM"
+TO_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${TO}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $TO"
+
+# --- kinds -------------------------------------------------------------------
+kinds="$(awk "$(cat "$FENCE_AWK")"'
+  md_fence($0) { next }
+  /^## / { insp = ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/); sec = 0; next }
+  !insp { next }
+  /^### / {
+    sec = 0
+    if ($0 ~ /^### Technical Tasks[[:space:]]*$/) sec = 1
+    else if ($0 ~ /^### Task [0-9A-Za-z]+\.E2E([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)/) sec = 2
+    next
+  }
+  !sec || $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] / { next }
+  sec == 2 && $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] Task / { next }
+  {
+    if (match($0, /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)[[:space:]]*$/)) {
+      v = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH)
+      sub(/^.*:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
+      n[v]++
+    } else n["untagged"]++
+  }
+  END { printf "%d %d %d %d\n", n["mechanical"], n["judgment"], n["operator"], n["untagged"] }
+' "$PLAN")"
+read -r K_MECH K_JUDG K_OPER K_UNTAGGED <<< "$kinds"
+[[ "$K_UNTAGGED" -eq 0 ]] || echo "WARN: $K_UNTAGGED task line(s) in $PLAN carry no kind: tag and are not counted" >&2
+
+# --- volume ------------------------------------------------------------------
+GIT_DIFF=(git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -M)
+SCRIPT_LINES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --numstat "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.sh' '*.py' '*.ts' '*.js' \
+  | awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { s += $1 + $2 } END { printf "%d\n", s }')"
+PROSE_BYTES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --unified=0 "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.md' \
+  | awk '
+      /^diff --git / { hunk = 0; next }
+      /^@@ / { hunk = 1; next }
+      # the marker byte stands in for the newline the diff line drops
+      hunk && /^[+-]/ { s += length($0) }
+      END { printf "%d\n", s }
+    ')"
+
+# --- model calls -------------------------------------------------------------
+FROM_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$FROM_SHA")"
+TO_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$TO_SHA")"
+MODEL_CALLS=""
+if [[ -f "$MODELINV" && -r "$MODELINV" ]]; then
+  MODEL_CALLS="$(jq -R --argjson lo "$FROM_TS" --argjson hi "$TO_TS" '
+      fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .primitive_id == "MODELINV")
+      | (.ts_utc // "") | tostring
+      | (try (sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601) catch null)
+      | select(. != null and . >= $lo and . <= $hi)
+    ' "$MODELINV" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
+else
+  echo "WARN: MODELINV log not found at $MODELINV; model calls n/a" >&2
+fi
+
+iso() { jq -nr --argjson t "$1" '$t | todateiso8601'; }
+
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  jq -n \
+    --arg from "$FROM_SHA" --arg to "$TO_SHA" \
+    --arg from_ts "$(iso "$FROM_TS")" --arg to_ts "$(iso "$TO_TS")" \
+    --arg plan "$PLAN" --arg modelinv "$MODELINV" \
+    --argjson mech "$K_MECH" --argjson judg "$K_JUDG" --argjson oper "$K_OPER" --argjson untagged "$K_UNTAGGED" \
+    --argjson script_lines "$SCRIPT_LINES" --argjson prose_bytes "$PROSE_BYTES" \
+    --arg calls "$MODEL_CALLS" \
+    '{from: $from, to: $to, window: {from: $from_ts, to: $to_ts}, sprint_plan: $plan,
+      kinds: {mechanical: $mech, judgment: $judg, operator: $oper, untagged: $untagged},
+      volume: {script_lines_changed: $script_lines, prose_bytes_changed: $prose_bytes,
+               model_calls: (if $calls == "" then null else ($calls | tonumber) end),
+               scope: "host", modelinv: $modelinv}}'
+else
+  printf 'kinds: mechanical %s · judgment %s · operator %s\n' "$K_MECH" "$K_JUDG" "$K_OPER"
+  printf "volume: script lines changed %s (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed %s (*.md) · model calls %s (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: %s\n" \
+    "$SCRIPT_LINES" "$PROSE_BYTES" "${MODEL_CALLS:-n/a}" "$MODELINV"
+fi

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# claude-stub.sh — stand-in for the `claude` CLI used by evals/tests/*.bats.
     3	# Records argv + selected env, optionally writes files into the cwd, and
     4	# emits a canned stream-json transcript so execute-agent.sh can be tested
     5	# without a model call.
     6	#
     7	#   STUB_ARGV_FILE   where "$@" is written (one arg per line)
     8	#   STUB_ENV_FILE    where selected env vars are written (KEY=VALUE)
     9	#   STUB_EVENTS_FILE stream-json lines to emit (default: a 2-write transcript)
    10	#   STUB_WRITE_<n>   "relative/path::content" files to create in the cwd
    11	#   STUB_EXIT        exit code (default 0)
    12	#   STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR  copy the cwd's CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .loa.config.yaml and
    13	#                    the --append-system-prompt-file there at start: the
    14	#                    sandbox exactly as the executor sees it (arm-toggles.bats)
    15	#   STUB_FAIL_COUNTER  a file holding N: while N > 0, decrement it and exit 1
    16	#                    with no result event (a transport failure; run-arms.bats)
    17	set -euo pipefail
    18	
    19	# `--version` (run-arms.sh records it in MANIFEST.json) has no side effects
    20	if [[ "${1:-}" == "--version" ]]; then echo "0.0.0 (claude-stub)"; exit 0; fi
    21	
    22	if [[ -n "${STUB_FAIL_COUNTER:-}" && -f "$STUB_FAIL_COUNTER" ]]; then
    23	  n="$(cat "$STUB_FAIL_COUNTER")"
    24	  if [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]]; then
    25	    echo $((n - 1)) > "$STUB_FAIL_COUNTER"
    26	    echo "stub: simulated transport failure (socket hang up)" >&2
    27	    exit 1
    28	  fi
    29	fi
    30	
    31	if [[ -n "${STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR:-}" ]]; then
    32	  mkdir -p "$STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR"
    33	  for p in CLAUDE.md .claude .loa.config.yaml; do
    34	    [[ -e "$p" ]] && cp -a "$p" "$STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR/"
    35	  done
    36	  prev=""
    37	  for a in "$@"; do
    38	    [[ "$prev" == "--append-system-prompt-file" ]] && cp "$a" "$STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR/system-prompt.md"
    39	    prev="$a"
    40	  done
    41	fi
    42	
    43	if [[ -n "${STUB_ARGV_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    44	  printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$STUB_ARGV_FILE"
    45	fi
    46	if [[ -n "${STUB_ENV_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    47	  {
    48	    printf 'PWD=%s\n' "$PWD"
    49	    for k in LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH HOME EVAL_MODEL TMPDIR GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN OPENAI_API_KEY AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY \
    50	             CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS; do
    51	      printf '%s=%s\n' "$k" "${!k:-}"
    52	    done
    53	  } > "$STUB_ENV_FILE"
    54	fi
    55	
    56	for var in "${!STUB_WRITE_@}"; do
    57	  spec="${!var}"
    58	  rel="${spec%%::*}"
    59	  body="${spec#*::}"
    60	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$rel")"
    61	  printf '%b' "$body" > "$rel"
    62	done
    63	
    64	if [[ -n "${STUB_EVENTS_FILE:-}" && -f "${STUB_EVENTS_FILE}" ]]; then
    65	  cat "$STUB_EVENTS_FILE"
    66	else
    67	  cat <<'EVENTS'
    68	{"type":"system","subtype":"init","model":"claude-sonnet-5"}
    69	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"tests/test_x.py","content":"def test_x(): assert False"}}]}}
    70	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"src/x.py","content":"X = 1"}}]}}
    71	{"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,"duration_ms":1234,"num_turns":3,"result":"done","total_cost_usd":0.0123,"usage":{"input_tokens":100,"output_tokens":42,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5,"cache_read_input_tokens":7},"modelUsage":{"claude-sonnet-5-20260401":{"inputTokens":100,"outputTokens":42,"cacheReadInputTokens":7,"cacheCreationInputTokens":5,"costUSD":0.0123}}}
    72	EVENTS
    73	fi
    74	
    75	exit "${STUB_EXIT:-0}"

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# evals/tests/arms-report.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-2, SDD D-2.3)
     4	#
     5	# report.sh --arms over a fixture results tree (the layout run-arms.sh
     6	# writes): the pre-registered verdicts, the bootstrap interval, refuted share,
     7	# missed labels, the refusal while STATUS.json is not complete and the
     8	# --partial header. Thresholds come from the real review-recall suite.
     9	# =============================================================================
    10	
    11	setup() {
    12	  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    13	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    14	  REPORT="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/report.sh"
    15	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ar.XXXXXX")"
    16	  R="$T/arms"; S="$R/review-recall"; B="$S/b1"
    17	  mkdir -p "$B"
    18	  jq -n '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", batch:"b1", dry_run:false, source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457",
    19	          model_id:"claude-fable-5-1", arms:["baseline","no_companion","no_karpathy","no_rule_files"], fixtures:["pr-01","pr-02","pr-03"], trials:3}' \
    20	    > "$B/MANIFEST.json"
    21	  status_file complete
    22	}
    23	
    24	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    25	
    26	status_file() {  # status_file <state>
    27	  jq -n --arg s "$1" '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", state:$s, batches:[{batch:"b1", state:$s}],
    28	                       source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457", model_id:"claude-fable-5-1"}' > "$S/STATUS.json"
    29	}
    30	
    31	# row <arm> <fixture> <trial> <recall> <missed-csv> [<cited> <refuted> <model> <source>]
    32	row() {
    33	  local arm="$1" fx="$2" t="$3" rc="$4" missed="$5" cited="${6:-4}" ref="${7:-1}"
    34	  local model="${8:-claude-fable-5-1}" src="${9:-864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457}"
    35	  mkdir -p "$B/$arm"
    36	  jq -cn --arg arm "$arm" --arg fx "$fx" --argjson t "$t" --argjson rc "$rc" --arg missed "$missed" \
    37	    --argjson cited "$cited" --argjson ref "$ref" --arg model "$model" --arg src "$src" \
    38	    '{status:"completed", arm:$arm, fixture:$fx, task_id:("review-" + $fx), trial:$t, model_id:$model, source_commit:$src,
    39	      executor:{model_id:$model, usage:{input_tokens:100, cache_read_input_tokens:900, output_tokens:0, cache_creation_input_tokens:0}},
    40	      graders:[{name:"recall-vs-defects.sh", details:{recall:$rc, planted:3,
    41	        detected:[], missed:($missed | split(",") | map(select(length > 0))),
    42	        findings_cited:$cited, findings_refuted:$ref}}]}' >> "$B/$arm/results.jsonl"
    43	}
    44	
    45	full_arm() {  # full_arm <arm> <recall> [<missed>] [<refuted>]
    46	  local fx t
    47	  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row "$1" "$fx" "$t" "$2" "${3:-}" 4 "${4:-1}"; done; done
    48	}

    59	  grep -E '^\| `no_companion` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q 'informational: yield only'
    60	  grep -E '^\| `baseline` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '(reference)'

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.5 (FR-2, SDD D-2.2)
     4	#
     5	# seed-corpus-from-record.sh over a tiny record tree built from
     6	# evals/tests/fixtures/seed-record/: a throwaway repo with base, head and fix
     7	# commits and a record branch carrying one round-1 review file. Proves: a
     8	# finding whose fix touches its file is kept; a finding whose file the fix
     9	# never touches is dropped by the rule; fix rows come from the fix hunks; a
    10	# finding carrying a secret is rejected; the approved-by header is required;
    11	# the labels stay out of the sandbox-copied fixture dir; SHA256SUMS covers it.
    12	# =============================================================================
    13	
    14	setup() {
    15	  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    16	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    17	  SEED="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh"
    18	  GRADER="$REPO_ROOT/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh"
    19	  FX="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/seed-record"
    20	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sc.XXXXXX")"
    21	  G="$T/repo"; C="$T/corpus"; K="$T/tasks"
    22	  mkdir -p "$G" "$C/pr-01" "$C/labels" "$K"
    23	  # the fake key is assembled here so no literal key shape is ever committed
    24	  FAKE_KEY="AKIA$(printf 'QZ%.0s' 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8)"
    25	  gc() { git -C "$G" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t "$@"; }
    26	  git -C "$G" init -q -b main
    27	  cp -R "$FX/base/." "$G/"; gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "base"
    28	  cp -R "$FX/head/." "$G/"; gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "feat: sprint-901 the input helper (round 1)"
    29	  cp -R "$FX/fix/." "$G/"; gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "fix: sprint-901 review round 1"
    30	  BASE="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD~2)"; HEAD_C="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD~1)"; FIX="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD)"
    31	  gc checkout -q --orphan record/cycle-901-a2a
    32	  git -C "$G" rm -rq --cached . ; find "$G" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name .git -exec rm -rf {} +
    33	  mkdir -p "$G/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-901"
    34	  sed "s/@SECRET@/$FAKE_KEY/" "$FX/engineer-feedback-r1.md.in" > "$G/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-901/engineer-feedback-r1.md"
    35	  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "record"; gc checkout -q main
    36	  # a minimal corpus: the instruction templates and the corpus spec header
    37	  echo "# Review instructions" > "$C/pr-01/REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md"
    38	  echo "# Audit instructions" > "$C/pr-01/AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md"
    39	  printf 'fixture\tkind\tcommit\tfile\tdefect_id\tseverity\tcategory\tmust_match\n' > "$C/corpus.tsv"
    40	  ARGS=(--repo "$G" --corpus "$C" --tasks-dir "$K" --base "$BASE" --head "$HEAD_C" --fix "$FIX" --feedback engineer-feedback-r1.md --out "$C/pr-90")
    41	}
    42	
    43	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    44	
    45	@test "SC-1 seeding builds the fixture; labels stay hidden; the fix-touches-file rule keeps a.sh and drops b.sh; fix rows come from the fix hunks" {
    46	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
    47	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    48	  for f in fixture.yaml head.diff PR.md REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md head/scripts/a.sh head/scripts/b.sh base/scripts/a.sh; do
    49	    [ -f "$C/pr-90/$f" ]
    50	  done
    51	  grep -q '^sprint: 901$' "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    52	  grep -q "^head_commit: \"$HEAD_C\"$" "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    53	  grep -q "^fix_commit: \"$FIX\"$" "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    54	  grep -q '^record_ref: "record/cycle-901-a2a"$' "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    55	  grep -q 'grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-901/engineer-feedback-r1.md' "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    56	  # the labels never sit in the directory the sandbox copies
    57	  [ -z "$(find "$C/pr-90" -name 'labels*' -o -name '*.dropped.txt')" ]
    58	  L="$C/labels/pr-90.tsv"
    59	  [ "$(head -1 "$L")" = "# approved-by: pending" ]
    60	  grep -qx "$(printf 'defect_id\tseverity\tcategory\tfile\tmust_match\tlabel_source\tsource')" "$L"
    61	  # kept: the a.sh finding (its fix touches a.sh), anchored where the fix inserts
    62	  # the missing check (after `local v="$1"`) and on the short function's definition
    63	  [ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L/ {print $4 "|" $6}' "$L" | sort -u)" = "scripts/a.sh|review" ]
    64	  awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L01-/ {print $5}' "$L" | grep -qxF 'local v="$1"'
    65	  awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L01-/ {print $5}' "$L" | grep -qxF 'check_input() {'
    66	  # dropped by the rule: b.sh (the fix never touches it); the prose finding; the previous-round section is never read
    67	  grep -q 'fix commit does not touch scripts/b.sh' "$C/labels/pr-90.dropped.txt"
    68	  grep -q 'no code locus' "$C/labels/pr-90.dropped.txt"
    69	  ! grep -q 'must never be read' "$L" "$C/labels/pr-90.dropped.txt"
    70	  # fix rows: one per fix hunk, on a.sh and c.sh, sourced fix/<sha>:<start>-<end>
    71	  [ "$(awk -F'\t' '$6 == "fix" {print $4}' "$L" | sort | tr '\n' ,)" = "scripts/a.sh,scripts/c.sh," ]
    72	  awk -F'\t' '$6 == "fix" {print $7}' "$L" | grep -qE "^fix/${FIX:0:12}:[0-9]+-[0-9]+$"
    73	  # the hidden manifest, the tasks, the corpus row and the freeze
    74	  M="$C/manifests/pr-90.json"
    75	  [ "$(jq -r '.approved' "$M")" = "false" ]
    76	  [ "$(jq -r '.defects | length' "$M")" = "1" ]
    77	  [ "$(jq -r '.fix_regions | length' "$M")" = "2" ]
    78	  [ "$(jq -r '.defects[0].label_source' "$M")" = "review" ]
    79	  [ -f "$K/review-recall/review-pr-90.yaml" ] && [ -f "$K/audit-recall/audit-pr-90.yaml" ]
    80	  [ "$(yq -r '.graders[0].args[0]' "$K/review-recall/review-pr-90.yaml")" = "pr-90" ]
    81	  grep -q "^pr-90	record	${HEAD_C:0:8}	labels/pr-90.tsv" "$C/corpus.tsv"
    82	  run "$SEED" --check --corpus "$C"
    83	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    84	}
    85	
    86	@test "SC-2 a finding carrying a secret is rejected without its text; nothing written carries the key and every file passes no-secrets.sh" {
    87	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
    88	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    89	  grep -q 'secret pattern in the finding text' "$C/labels/pr-90.dropped.txt"
    90	  ! grep -rqF "$FAKE_KEY" "$C"
    91	  ! awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L/ {print $4}' "$C/labels/pr-90.tsv" | grep -q 'c.sh'
    92	  run bash "$REPO_ROOT/evals/graders/no-secrets.sh" "$C"
    93	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    94	}
    95	
    96	@test "SC-3 recall-vs-defects.sh grades the seeded label: the anchor detects it, a fix region is not refuted, an unrelated line is" {
    97	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
    98	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    99	  local at; at="$(jq -r '.defects[0].anchor_line' "$C/manifests/pr-90.json")"
   100	  W="$T/ws"; mkdir -p "$W"
   101	  printf '%s\n' "- HIGH head/scripts/a.sh:$at accepts an empty value" "- LOW head/scripts/c.sh:3 prints the token" \
   102	    "- LOW head/scripts/b.sh:2 loops forever" > "$W/review.md"
   103	  EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR="$C/manifests" run "$GRADER" "$W" pr-90 review.md
   104	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   105	  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.details.recall == 1')" = "true" ]
   106	  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.details.findings_cited')" = "3" ]
   107	  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.details.findings_refuted')" = "1" ]
   108	}
   109	
   110	@test "SC-4 the approved-by header is required; --approve records the approver, marks the manifest approved and refreezes" {
   111	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
   112	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   113	  L="$C/labels/pr-90.tsv"
   114	  cp "$L" "$T/keep.tsv"
   115	  tail -n +2 "$T/keep.tsv" > "$L"
   116	  run "$SEED" --build-manifest pr-90 --corpus "$C"
   117	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   118	  grep -q 'approved-by' <<<"$output"
   119	  cp "$T/keep.tsv" "$L"
   120	  run "$SEED" --approve pr-90 --by "lead 2026-10-14" --corpus "$C"
   121	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   122	  [ "$(head -1 "$L")" = "# approved-by: lead 2026-10-14" ]
   123	  [ "$(jq -r '.approved' "$C/manifests/pr-90.json")" = "true" ]
   124	  [ "$(jq -r '.approved_by' "$C/manifests/pr-90.json")" = "lead 2026-10-14" ]
   125	  run "$SEED" --check --corpus "$C"
   126	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   127	  run "$SEED" --approve pr-90 --by 'x;$(id)' --corpus "$C"
   128	  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   129	}

   131	@test "SC-5 curation.tsv drops or re-anchors a label on every re-seed" {
   132	  printf 'fixture\tlabel\taction\tvalue\treason\npr-90\tL01\tanchors\treturn 0\ttest re-anchor\n' > "$C/labels/curation.tsv"
   133	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
   134	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   135	  [ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L01-/ {print $5}' "$C/labels/pr-90.tsv")" = "return 0" ]
   136	  # dropping the only label leaves a gap: nothing stale survives, the reason is kept
   137	  printf 'fixture\tlabel\taction\tvalue\treason\npr-90\tL01\tdrop\t-\ttest drop\n' > "$C/labels/curation.tsv"
   138	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
   139	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

   141	  [ ! -e "$C/pr-90" ] && [ ! -e "$C/labels/pr-90.tsv" ] && [ ! -e "$C/manifests/pr-90.json" ] && [ ! -e "$K/review-recall/review-pr-90.yaml" ]
   142	  grep -q '^# pr-90 sprint-901: no record fixture' "$C/corpus.tsv"

+# .claude/data/floor.yaml — the one tracked floor source (cycle-129 SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166).
+#
+# The floor is the set of guards, config keys and files no profile, knob or
+# cycle task may weaken. Readers:
+#   - .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh and tests/unit/guard-origins.bats: the
+#     `floor: true` rows of .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml equal floor_guards.
+#   - tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats: every floor_files entry (and the corpus
+#     rows named under floor_corpus) is byte-identical to origin/main.
+#   - tests/unit/profile-floor.bats (Sprint 2): profiles.yaml names no floor_keys.
+# Both bats suites pin this file's sha256; an edit fails until the pin is
+# deliberately updated in the same change (see the FLOOR_SHA256 constant).
+schema_version: 1
+
+floor_guards:
+  - fence:FR-1.2b
+  - fence:FR-SZ
+  - fence:FR-SZ-COPY
+  - fence:FR-SZ-DD
+  - fence:FR-SZ-EXTRACT
+  - fence:FR-SZ-INPLACE
+  - fence:FR-SZ-INTERP
+  - fence:FR-SZ-LINK
+  - fence:FR-SZ-REDIR
+  - fence:FR-SZ-TEE
+  - fence:FR-SZ2
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-COPY
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-INPLACE
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-REDIR
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-RM
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-TEE
+  - gate:verdict-derive
+  - gate:adversarial-review-gate
+  - policy:permission-deny-list
+  - policy:verdict-one-way-rule
+  - policy:operator-only-commands
+
+floor_keys:
+  - flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled
+  - flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled
+  - "flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice"
+  - "destructive_command_guard.*"
+  - "implement_gate.*"
+  - hounfour.locality
+
+# Paths whose bytes must not change relative to origin/main during a cycle.
+floor_files:
+  - .claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh
+  - .claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh
+  - .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json
+  - .claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt

+floor_corpus:

+    - "FR-SZ*"

+# .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml — the guard origin map (cycle-129 SDD D-1.1, §3.1).
+#
+# The one hand-written input of the guard register. `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh`
+# enumerates the guards from the repository (hook commands in .claude/settings.json,
+# `# @guard fence:<id>` markers in block-destructive-bash.sh, `# @guard validator:<id>`
+# markers in validate-artifact.sh) and fails (exit 5) when one has no row here, when a
+# row here resolves to nothing, or when a row's origin is empty. It then writes the
+# tracked structural register grimoires/loa/guards.md and the untracked host yield
+# .run/guard-yield.{md,json}. Regenerate after editing: .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table
+#
+# Row fields:
+#   id             hook:<path under .claude/hooks> (scripts outside it: hook:scripts/<name>),
+#                  fence:<pattern id>, validator:<type>.<rule>, gate:<name>, policy:<name>;
+#                  ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$
+#   kind           hook | fence | validator | gate | policy
+#   class          harness (the model cannot override it) | script (a script checks or
+#                  reports) | prose (the model is asked to comply)
+#   status         active | dormant (armed only by the env var named in knob) |
+#                  telemetry (observes and logs, never refuses)
+#   origin         {kind: kf|issue|finding|cycle|design, ref: <non-empty>}; design rows
+#                  cite the commit that added the guard (git log --follow --diff-filter=A)
+#   knob           the config key or env var that arms, relaxes or disables it, or none
+#   floor          true exactly for the ids in .claude/data/floor.yaml floor_guards
+#   registrations  hook rows: every "<Event>:<matcher>" (or "<Event>" when the
+#                  registration has no matcher) from .claude/settings.json; [] otherwise
+#   script         gate and policy rows: the file that implements it (must exist)
+#   note           one line; the hooks-reference table's Purpose column for hook rows
+schema_version: 1
+guards:
+  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- hooks
+  - id: hook:scripts/upgrade-health-check.sh
+    kind: hook
+    class: script
+    status: active
+    origin: {kind: design, ref: "v1.5.0 692aa617"}
+    knob: none
+    floor: false
+    registrations: ["Setup"]
+    note: "Post-install and post-upgrade health check of the framework mount"
+  - id: hook:scripts/check-updates.sh
+    kind: hook
+    class: script
+    status: active
+    origin: {kind: design, ref: "v0.14.0 1f448140"}
+    knob: update_check.enabled
+    floor: false
+    registrations: ["SessionStart"]
+    note: "Notify when a newer framework release exists (cached; LOA_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=1 silences it)"
+  - id: hook:session-start/loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh
+    kind: hook
+    class: script
+    status: active
+    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-098 FR-L6 (#771)"}
+    knob: structured_handoff.enabled
+    floor: false
+    registrations: ["SessionStart"]
+    note: "Surface unread L6 structured handoffs inside a data fence"
+  - id: hook:session-start/loa-l7-surface-soul.sh
+    kind: hook
+    class: script
+    status: active
+    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-098 FR-L7"}
+    knob: soul_identity_doc.enabled
+    floor: false
+    registrations: ["SessionStart"]
+    note: "Surface the L7 soul identity document inside a data fence"
+  - id: hook:session-start/loa-run-mode-session-title.sh
+    kind: hook
+    class: script
+    status: active
+    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-114 FR-9"}

    10	---
    11	
    12	# Git Stash Safety
    13	
    14	`git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry. Combined with output-swallowing (`| tail -N`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`) this produces silent data loss that looks like success.
    15	
    16	**Mechanically enforced since cycle-122**: `block-destructive-bash.sh` pattern `FR-1.2b` BLOCKS `git stash push/pop/apply` combined with `| tail`/`| head`, `|| true`, or `2>/dev/null` in the same statement — the block message is the repair prompt. This file keeps only the interface and the judgment rules a fence cannot express.
    17	
    18	## The safe interface
    19	
    20	```bash
    21	source .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh
    22	stash_with_guard "pre-check" -- run_linter src/   # count-delta enforced, full output surfaced, exit propagated
    23	```
    24	
    25	Or sidestep stashing entirely with a worktree (no index-shift window):
    26	
    27	```bash
    28	worktree_path="$(mktemp -d)/loa-check"
    29	git worktree add "$worktree_path" HEAD
    30	(cd "$worktree_path" && run_linter src/)
    31	git worktree remove "$worktree_path"
    32	```
    33	
    34	## Judgment rules the fence cannot express
    35	
    36	- MUST NOT combine `git stash -k` with pre-commit-wrapped operations (the internal `--keep-index` collision is invisible to a command-string fence) — use a worktree.
    37	- SHOULD reach for `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` BEFORE any `git gc` when recovery is needed — orphaned stashes survive in the object DB only until the next prune.
    38	
    39	## Origin
    40	
    41	- Defect: [#555](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/555) — 4 Edit-tool NOTES.md updates lost to the hazard pattern; recovered only because `git gc --prune=now` hadn't run. Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557).
    42	- The hazard shape recurred live during cycle-122 itself (a `git stash pop >/dev/null 2>&1` during a baseline check — caught, verified lossless, and turned into the FR-1.2b fence the same day).
    43	
    44	## Related rules
    45	
    46	- [shell-conventions.md](shell-conventions.md) — heredoc safety, strict-mode patterns.

    34	## Enforcement
    35	
    36	`.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh` checks this invariant on every SKILL.md. A violation exits with code 1 and message:
    37	
    38	> agent type '<name>' excludes Write/Edit tools but skill declares write capability …
    39	
    40	The allowlist is maintained in `.claude/data/agent-types.yaml` (one `write_capable` flag per agent type); the script loads the `true` entries into `WRITE_CAPABLE_AGENTS` and falls back to `general-purpose` alone when the file is missing, unparsable, or lists no `write_capable: true` entry. Adding a new write-capable agent type is intentionally a one-line edit with reviewer visibility.
    41	
    42	## Mechanical C-PROC-001 enforcement via `disallowed-tools` (cycle-114 FR-4)
    43	
    44	`disallowed-tools` frontmatter (Claude Code ≥2.1.152) removes tools from the
    45	model while a skill is active — a harness-level barrier that instructions
    46	cannot override. Cycle-114 uses it to make C-PROC-001 ("NEVER write application
    47	code outside `/implement`") mechanical for review skills rather than prose-only.
    48	
    49	| Skill class | `disallowed-tools` | Why |
    50	|-------------|--------------------|-----|
    51	| Pure-review (`write_files: false`, no report artifacts) | `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit` | Never writes anything — remove the write tools outright |
    52	| Sprint review/audit (`reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit` | Write STATE-zone feedback/checkmarks/COMPLETED markers, run the allowed verdict check and run `adversarial-review.sh` (forks the provider CLIs, appends the `.run` cost and MODELINV ledgers, moves the previous round's a2a envelope aside as `.prev`, writes the new one; review also runs `qmd-context-query.sh`); System remains `none` and App remains `read` |
    53	| Report-authoring review (`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit`, `Bash(git add/commit/push *)` | Legitimately write STATE-zone reports/vision/lore, so `Write` is retained; app-code prevention is governed by **zones**, and the implementation-only git mutations are removed |
    54	
    55	**`REVIEW_WRITE_EXCEPTIONS`** (in `validate-skill-capabilities.sh`):
    56	`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`, `spiraling`, `autonomous-agent`,
    57	`run-bridge`, `run-mode`, `reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`. These `role: review` skills keep `Write` by design —
    58	the adversarial/report authors write STATE-zone artifacts, and the autonomous
    59	orchestrators dispatch implementation through the harness (which runs inside
    60	`/implement`, where writes are sanctioned). The validator emits a WARN for any *other* `role: review`
    61	skill that declares `write_files: true` without disallowing `Write` — surfacing
    62	a new C-PROC-001 gap at lint time. `disallowed-tools` is tool-granular, not
    63	path-granular; it cannot express "no `src/` writes but yes `grimoires/` writes",
    64	which is why report-authoring skills rely on zones for path-level control.
    65	
    66	## Scope
    67	
    68	Applies to every `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md`. The lint runs as part of the normal validation suite (`bats tests/unit/skill-capabilities.bats`).
    69	
    70	## Origin
    71	
    72	- Defect: [#553](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/553) — `/architect` and `/sprint-plan` produced correct output but refused to write their target files. Three independent reproductions across two repos.
    73	- Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557) — Tier 1 cycle-083 framework boundary fixes.
    74	- Sprint: `sprint-bug-102` — test-first patch landing the invariant lint + the three frontmatter fixes.
    75	
    76	## Related rules
    77	
    78	- [zone-system.md](zone-system.md) — `.claude/` is framework-managed; SKILL.md edits require cycle-level authorization.
    79	- [shell-conventions.md](shell-conventions.md) — file-creation safety when authoring SKILL.md via heredoc.
====BASE
# Git Stash Safety

`git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry. Combined with output-swallowing (`| tail -N`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`) this produces silent data loss that looks like success.

**Mechanically enforced since cycle-122**: `block-destructive-bash.sh` pattern `FR-1.2b` BLOCKS `git stash push/pop/apply` combined with `| tail`/`| head`, `|| true`, or `2>/dev/null` in the same statement — the block message is the repair prompt. This file keeps only the interface and the judgment rules a fence cannot express.

## The safe interface

```bash
source .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh
stash_with_guard "pre-check" -- run_linter src/   # count-delta enforced, full output surfaced, exit propagated
```

Or sidestep stashing entirely with a worktree (no index-shift window):


# Skill Frontmatter Invariants

SKILL.md frontmatter keys interact across two permission layers: the skill's own `capabilities` / `allowed-tools` declarations, and Claude Code's per-agent-type tool allowlist. When the two disagree, the agent-type allowlist wins — silently. Agents that declare write capability but dispatch through a read-only agent type produce correct output and then refuse to persist it.

## The invariant

When a skill declares write capability — either `capabilities.write_files: true` OR `allowed-tools` listing `Write`/`Edit` — it MUST NOT set `agent:` to a type that excludes those tools.

Allowed: omit the `agent:` key (skill runs in the caller's context), or set `agent:` to a write-capable type (`general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork`).

## Agent type tool allowlists

| Agent type | Write / Edit / NotebookEdit | Use for |
|------------|-----------------------------|---------|
| `general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork` | ✓ all tools | Skills that author files |

## Pre-Execution Guardrails (mechanized)

Skip this section when `.loa.config.yaml` has `guardrails.input.enabled: false` or env
`LOA_GUARDRAILS_ENABLED=false`.

Otherwise: write the user's invocation prompt/args to a temp file (Write tool), then run
`.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill implementing-tasks --mode ${LOA_RUN_MODE:-interactive} --file <temp-file>`

| Outcome | Action |
|---------|--------|
| JSON `action: "BLOCK"` | HALT; report the script's `reason` to the user |
| JSON `action: "PROCEED"` or `"WARN"` | Continue (the script logs) |
| Script missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output | Continue (fail-open) |

Never pass prompt text as a bash argv (quote-blindness FP class) — always via `--file`.

ARM_EVIDENCE='{}'
_evidence() { ARM_EVIDENCE="$(jq -c --arg k "$1" --arg v "$2" '. + {($k): $v}' <<<"$ARM_EVIDENCE")"; }

apply_toggles() {
  local key val
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
    if [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)" >&2; return 2
    fi
    case "$key" in
      companion_voice)
        local cfg="$WORKSPACE/.loa.config.yaml"
        [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice = false | .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice = false' "$cfg" \
          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle: yq failed on the sandbox config" >&2; return 2; }
        [[ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice' "$cfg")" == "false" ]] \
          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle did not take effect" >&2; return 2; }
        _evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
        ;;
      karpathy_block)
        local k="$WORKSPACE/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n
        [[ -f "$k" ]] || { echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no sandbox CLAUDE.loa.md" >&2; return 2; }
        n="$(_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles')"
        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then
          echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed" >&2; return 2
        fi
        local cj="$WORKSPACE/.claude/data/constraints.json"
        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then
          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" && mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"
        fi
        _evidence karpathy_block "removed ${n} lines from CLAUDE.loa.md"
        ;;
      rule_files)
        local r gone=""
        for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
          if [[ -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]]; then rm -f "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r"; gone="$gone $r"; fi
          [[ ! -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]] || { echo "ERROR: rule_files toggle: $r still present" >&2; return 2; }
        done
        _evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"
        ;;
      audit_delta_instruction)
        local s="$WORKSPACE/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
        [[ -f "$s" ]] || { echo "ERROR: audit_delta_instruction toggle: no sandbox auditing-security/SKILL.md" >&2; return 2; }
        _drop_paragraph "$s" "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" \
          || { echo "ERROR: audit_delta_instruction toggle: no delta paragraph found in the sandbox SKILL.md" >&2; return 2; }
        _evidence audit_delta_instruction "removed $(wc -c < "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" | tr -d ' ') bytes (.eval/arm-removed.txt)"
        ;;
      *) echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' declares unknown toggle '$key'" >&2; return 2 ;;

apply_toggles() {
  local key val
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
    if [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)" >&2; return 2
    fi
    case "$key" in
      companion_voice)
        local cfg="$WORKSPACE/.loa.config.yaml"
        [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice = false | .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice = false' "$cfg" \
          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle: yq failed on the sandbox config" >&2; return 2; }
        [[ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice' "$cfg")" == "false" ]] \
          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle did not take effect" >&2; return 2; }
        _evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
        ;;
      karpathy_block)
        local k="$WORKSPACE/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n
        [[ -f "$k" ]] || { echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no sandbox CLAUDE.loa.md" >&2; return 2; }
        n="$(_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles')"
        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then

        fi
        local cj="$WORKSPACE/.claude/data/constraints.json"
        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then

        fi

        ;;

== rubrics
# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

---

## Architecture Rubrics

### ARCH-MO: Modularity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Clear separation of concerns. Well-defined interfaces. Easy to modify/extend. |
| 4 | Good modularity with minor coupling issues. |
| 3 | Some modularity but tight coupling in places. |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# validate-artifact.sh — Parameterized planning-artifact validator (C10)
# =============================================================================
# Part of cycle-119 "mechanical floor". One grep-based, fail-closed validator
# for the four planning artifact types, wired as a final-phase MUST step in
# discovering-requirements / designing-architecture / planning-sprints /
# bug-triaging.
#
# Usage:
#   validate-artifact.sh --type prd|sdd|sprint|bug-triage|translation|decisions|map|spike|glossary --file <path>
#                        [--base-file <path>] [--ledger <path>] [--json]
#
# Per-type checks (see designing-architecture/planning-sprints/bug-triaging
# SKILL.md + their resources/templates/*.md for the source-of-truth shapes):
#   prd:        every '## ' section has a '> Sources:' line in its body;
#               counts [ASSUMPTION fact|decision] and bare [ASSUMPTION] tags
#               (outside code); a bare tag WARNs, and fails for PRDs dated on or
#               after BARE_ASSUMPTION_FAILS_FROM; each [ASSUMPTION decision] line
#               and each **Deferred:** line must cite a DEC row in the ledger
#               (--ledger, default grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml) whose source
#               names the PRD: FAIL in an unattended context, WARN otherwise
#   sdd:        the 10 required numbered H2 sections are present (derived
#               from designing-architecture/SKILL.md Phase 4 + its
#               sdd-template.md); WARN (never fails) on bare framework names
#               with no version-shaped token nearby; WARN on an Open Questions
#               row marked Resolved without a DEC id in its DEC column
#   sprint:     every '## Sprint N' block has its 8 required sections; every
#               goal ID (G-N) referenced in the plan appears in the '##
#               Appendix' goal table; WARN if the final sprint has no
....
sprint: plans dated from 2026-10-14 end every task line with
  ' · kind: mechanical|judgment|operator' (older plans WARN).

Exit codes:
  0  pass (WARN-level info may still be printed)
  1  fail (exact repair text on stderr)
  2  usage error (missing arguments, unknown type, file not found)
EOF
}

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --type) TYPE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --file) FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --base-file) BASE_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --ledger) LEDGER_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --json) JSON_OUTPUT=true; shift ;;
        -h|--help) show_help; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; show_help >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

if [[ -z "$TYPE" || -z "$FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: --type and --file are required" >&2
    show_help >&2
    exit 2
fi

case "$TYPE" in
    prd|sdd|sprint|bug-triage|translation|decisions|map|spike|glossary) ;;
    *) echo "Error: --type must be one of prd|sdd|sprint|bug-triage|translation|decisions|map|spike|glossary (got: $TYPE)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

if [[ "$TYPE" == "translation" ]]; then
    # translation accepts a single .md file OR a directory of them.
    if [[ ! -e "$FILE" ]]; then
        echo "Error: file not found: $FILE" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
elif [[ ! -f "$FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: file not found: $FILE" >&2
    exit 2
fi

violations=()
warnings=()
info_lines=()

# =============================================================================
# prd
# =============================================================================
....
# @guard validator:sprint.sections
SPRINT_REQUIRED_SECTIONS=(
    "Sprint Goal"
    "Deliverables"
    "Acceptance Criteria"
    "Technical Tasks"
    "Dependencies"
    "Risks & Mitigation"
    "Success Metrics"
)
SPRINT_WARN_SECTIONS=(
    "Security Considerations"
)

validate_sprint() {
    local sprint_headings
    sprint_headings=$(grep -nE '^## Sprint [0-9]' -- "$FILE" || true)

    if [[ -z "$sprint_headings" ]]; then
        violations+=("no '## Sprint N' blocks found — sprint.md must contain at least one sprint block")
        return
    fi

    local last_sprint_heading="" last_sprint_lineno=0
    while IFS=: read -r lineno heading; do
        [[ -z "$lineno" ]] && continue
        last_sprint_heading="$heading"
        last_sprint_lineno="$lineno"
        local block
        block=$(awk -v start="$lineno" '
            NR > start && /^## Sprint [0-9]/ { exit }
            NR > start { print }
        ' < "$FILE")
        local sec
        for sec in "${SPRINT_REQUIRED_SECTIONS[@]}"; do
            if ! grep -qE "^### ($sec)\$" <<< "$block"; then
                violations+=("sprint block '${heading# }' (line $lineno) is missing required section '### $sec' — see planning-sprints/resources/templates/sprint-template.md")
            fi
        done
        for sec in "${SPRINT_WARN_SECTIONS[@]}"; do
            if ! grep -qE "^### ($sec)\$" <<< "$block"; then
                warnings+=("sprint block '${heading# }' (line $lineno) has no '### $sec' section — recommended for security-relevant sprints")
            fi
        done
    done <<< "$sprint_headings"

    # @guard validator:sprint.goal-ids
    # Goal ID coverage: every G-N referenced in the plan body must appear in
    # a goal-mapping table under any '## Appendix' section.
    local appendix_body
    appendix_body=$(awk '
        /^## Appendix/ { found=1; next }
        found && /^## / { found=0 }
        found { print }
    ' < "$FILE")

    local body_goal_ids
    body_goal_ids=$(grep -oE 'G-[0-9]+' -- "$FILE" | sort -u || true)
    if [[ -n "$body_goal_ids" ]]; then
        while IFS= read -r gid; do
            [[ -z "$gid" ]] && continue
            if ! grep -qwF "$gid" <<< "$appendix_body"; then
                violations+=("goal ID $gid appears in the plan but not in any '## Appendix' goal table — add a row for $gid")
            fi
        done <<< "$body_goal_ids"
    fi

    validate_sprint_deferred
    validate_sprint_seams
    validate_sprint_kinds
    validate_sprint_beads

    # Final sprint E2E/validation task (WARN only).
    local last_block
    last_block=$(awk -v start="$last_sprint_lineno" 'NR > start { print }' < "$FILE")
    if ! grep -qiE 'E2E|end-to-end' <<< "$last_block"; then
        warnings+=("final sprint block '${last_sprint_heading# }' has no E2E/end-to-end validation task")
    fi
}

# =============================================================================

    15	globs() { frontmatter "$1" | yq eval '.paths[]' -; }

diff --git a/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md b/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
index a6e116bf..b3a69cf6 100644
--- a/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+++ b/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
@@ -50,11 +50,15 @@ ## Language
 **Jack in**: To start an autonomous run under run mode; a run that has finished or been stopped for good has jacked out.
 _Aliases_: jack out
 
+**Judgment**: The task kind for work that needs reading and a decision; it ships as prose or a reviewed artifact, and its sprint task line ends with kind: judgment.
+
 **Kaironic**: Stopping at the right moment rather than after a fixed count: an iterative review loop ends when successive passes stop finding material issues.
 _Avoid_: converged
 
 **Karpathy principles**: The four working rules applied on every code-touching turn: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes and goal-driven verification.
 
+**Kind counts**: The release-notes line that counts a cycle's sprint tasks by kind (mechanical, judgment and operator), read from the tagged task lines of its sprint plan.
+
 **Known failure**: A recorded degradation with its symptom, the attempts made and a reading guide, consulted before triage so that prior dead ends are not retried.
 _Aliases_: KF
 
@@ -62,6 +66,10 @@ ## Language
 
 **Map epic**: The epic bead that parents an effort's decision tickets, paired with a map document of its destination, decisions so far, fog and exclusions; run mode never implements it.
 
+**Mechanical**: The task kind for work a script could do reliably; it ships as code with tests, and a review flags a mechanical task delivered as prose the model re-executes.
+
+**Operator**: The human who owns the project and its decisions; as a task kind, work that belongs to that human, which a review flags when it was completed unattended without a decision:unblock ticket or a DEC row.
+
 **Round**: One frontier of interview questions asked together and answered together.
 
 **Run mode**: Unattended execution of a sprint plan with a circuit breaker, wrapping implement, review and audit in a loop. Its states are running, halted and jacked out.
@@ -78,4 +86,6 @@ ## Language
 
 **Voice**: The party a decision or finding is attributed to: the operator, the agent, Flatline or dissent.

The corpus is built from this repository's own `fix(...)` commits by `fixtures/build-review-corpus.sh`
(each defect PR turns fixed code back into the buggy parent; comment-only lines the fix added are
stripped so the diff removes code, never a confession) and frozen by `review-prs/SHA256SUMS`
(`build-review-corpus.sh --verify`). Hidden manifests (`review-prs/manifests/`, `implement-tasks/expectations/`)
are never copied into a sandbox. A defect counts as detected when the output cites the defect's file and
a line within ±3 of the manifest anchor — no fuzzy adjudication.

```bash
# arm A on the pre-change prompt tree (a worktree), arm B on the current tree, same model + effort
EVAL_PROMPT_TREE=/path/to/worktree EVAL_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5 EVAL_EFFORT=medium \
  ./evals/harness/run-eval.sh --suite review-recall --trusted --concurrency 2
./evals/harness/compare.sh --results <arm-a>/results.jsonl --suite review-recall --prompt-tree /path/to/worktree \
  --update-baseline --reason "arm A" --baseline-out evals/baselines/review-recall.baseline.yaml
./evals/harness/compare.sh --ab --arm-a <arm-a-run-dir> --arm-b <arm-b-run-dir> --metric recall
```

`compare.sh` refuses a baseline whose `prompt_tree_sha` equals the tree under comparison, whose
`captured_at_commit` is not a descendant of the suite's `ab.floor_commit`, or whose `corpus_sha256`
drifted (`evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats`). Tests: `evals/tests/{execute-agent,eval-recall-grader,implement-discipline-grader,recall-baseline-freshness}.bats`.

## Control arms and the record corpus (cycle-129 FR-2)

Each recall suite pre-registers control arms in `ab.arms` (review: `baseline`, `no_companion`
(informational), `no_karpathy`, `no_rule_files`; audit: `baseline`, `no_audit_delta`) and the verdict rule
in `ab.threshold`. `execute-agent.sh` applies an arm (`LOA_EVAL_ARM`) to the sandbox copy only, after
materialisation and immediately before the executor starts, and fails the trial (exit 2) when a toggle
cannot take effect; `executor.json` records `arm`, `arm_toggles`, `arm_evidence`, `source_commit`,
`models_used` and `refusal_fallbacks`. The executor never inherits the calling Claude Code session's
coupling, and its subagent model is pinned to `EVAL_MODEL`.

The record fixtures `pr-11` … `pr-18` are the round-1 states of sprints 247–254, built by
`harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh` from `review-prs/record-pairs.tsv` and the `record/cycle-12x-a2a`
branches. A feedback finding becomes a label only when the fix commit touches the file it cites. Labels
live in the hidden `review-prs/labels/pr-NN.tsv` (never in the sandbox-copied `pr-NN/`), every drop is
explained in `labels/pr-NN.dropped.txt`, and hand curation is the data file `labels/curation.tsv`,
re-applied on every seed. `fix` rows (the hunks the fix commit changed) feed the grader's refuted share
only. A label file is approved with `seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve pr-NN --by "<who> <date>"`;
`run-arms.sh` refuses unapproved fixtures unless `--allow-unapproved`.

```bash
# one suite, one batch, against a detached worktree pinned at the source commit
./evals/harness/run-arms.sh --suite review-recall --arms baseline,no_companion,no_karpathy,no_rule_files \
  --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,pr-03,pr-04,pr-05,pr-06,pr-07,pr-08 --trials 3 --source-commit 864069f2 --dry-run
./evals/harness/report.sh --arms            # refuses until STATUS.json is complete; --partial for interim
./evals/harness/compare.sh --ab --arm-a evals/results/arms/review-recall/<batch>/baseline \
  --arm-b evals/results/arms/review-recall/<batch>/no_karpathy --metric recall
```

content.text:
I have what I need; the repros confirmed two of the seed-script claims and the toggle-resolution claim, and the stray-file worry was moot (the `cd` failure short-circuited the heredoc; `/workspace` is clean, only the pre-existing `review.md`).

## Confirmation of the known items

- (a) **Confirmed.** `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:263-266` — `gone` stays empty when neither rule file exists and `_evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"` returns 0; no `return 2`. `arm-toggles.bats` AT-4 (lines 114-124) only tests the files-present case; AT-9 (170-179) covers karpathy/audit-delta absence but not rule_files.
- (b) **Confirmed.** `run-arms.sh:314-315` greps `network|...|5[0-9][0-9] ` over `$out` = `.eval/agent-output.json`, which `execute-agent.sh:358-362` writes as the verbatim `result` event including the model's final text. Only the stub's stderr "socket hang up" path is tested (`claude-stub.sh:26`, `run-arms.bats:98-128`).
- (c) **Confirmed.** `run_trial` spans `run-arms.sh:319-384` (66 lines), 4-deep nesting at 353-360.
- (d) **Confirmed.** `suite_report` spans `arms-report.py:176-343` (168 lines).

## New findings

**`head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:336-340` — HIGH, confidence medium — an ambient `LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES` in the operator's shell silently overrides every arm's pre-registered toggles, baseline included.**
```
EVAL_PROMPT_TREE="$WORKTREE" EVAL_MODEL="$MODEL" LOA_EVAL_ARM="$arm" LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE="$SUITE_FILE" \
  LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT="$SRC_FULL" LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 \
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/execute-agent.sh" ...
```
`execute-agent.sh:163-167` prefers `LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES` over the suite file whenever it is non-empty, and run-arms never unsets or overrides it. An operator who exported it for an AT-11-style manual run (`{"rule_files":false}`) then launches a batch: `baseline`, `no_karpathy` and `no_rule_files` all run with exactly that toggle set, rows still carry the plan's `arm` id, and `arms-report.py` (which keys on `arm`, never on `arm_toggles`) reports "no recall loss" for `no_karpathy` from two identical configurations. `run-arms.bats:31` explicitly `unset LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES`, so the test suite cannot see this. Related: `write_manifest` hard-codes `effort: "task/skill default"` (line 197) although an inherited `EVAL_EFFORT` changes the real effort. Fix: `unset LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES` (or pass `LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES=` explicitly) in the per-trial env at 336, and record `EVAL_EFFORT`/`EVAL_MAX_TURNS` in MANIFEST.json.

**`head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:178-186` — MEDIUM, confidence high — a declared non-baseline arm whose entry lacks a `toggles` key resolves to `{}` and runs as the baseline under its own id.**
```
t="$(ARM="$ARM" yq -o=json -I=0 '[.ab.arms[] | select(.id == strenv(ARM))][0].toggles // {}' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null)"
...
if [[ "$found" -eq 0 || -z "$t" || "$t" == "null" ]]; then
```
Verified in a scratch suite: an arm with no `toggles:` yields `found=1 toggles={}`, `apply_toggles` loops zero times, exit 0. A typo (`toggle:` for `toggles:`) in a future suite edit produces a full batch of identically configured "arms" and a clean verdict, directly contradicting the header's "an arm never silently runs as its baseline" (lines 65-66). No bats test covers it (AT-10 covers undeclared arm / unknown toggle only). Fix: after resolution, `[[ "$ARM" != baseline && "$t" == "{}" ]]` → exit 2.

**`head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:251-257` and `:264-265` — MEDIUM, confidence high — a second run into an existing batch with a different `--arms`/`--fixtures` set overwrites MANIFEST.json and resets STATUS.json, orphaning the earlier arms' results.**
```
  [[ "$prev_src" == "$SRC_FULL" && "$prev_model" == "$MODEL" ]] \
    || die "batch $BATCH already holds results for source $prev_src / model $prev_model; use another --batch"
fi
write_manifest "$BATCH_DIR/MANIFEST.json" false
...
DONE=() FAILED=() PLANNED=()
```
Only source/model are compared; arms and fixtures are not. Run batch B with `baseline,no_karpathy`, then re-run B with `--arms no_rule_files` to add an arm: MANIFEST.json now lists only `no_rule_files`, `arms-report.py:206-211` reads `results.jsonl` only for arms named in the manifest, so the baseline rows in `B/baseline/results.jsonl` vanish from the report ("no baseline arm" → inconclusive, or if another batch supplies a baseline, the batch's own baseline is silently excluded), and the batch STATUS.json `per_arm` loses the earlier counters. `run-arms.bats` RA-5 (144-150) only tests the model-mismatch refusal. Fix: also refuse (or merge) when `.arms`/`.fixtures`/`.trials` differ from the existing manifest, and never reset counters for arms already present.

**`head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:135-155` — MEDIUM, confidence high — `verify_corpus` only hashes files listed in SHA256SUMS; a file added to `pr-NN/` is copied into every sandbox with no "drift".**
```
for line in raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines():
    ...
    digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
    ...
    if not os.path.isfile(p) or hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != digest:
        bad.append(rel)
```

# Sprint 1 Security Audit Feedback

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)
**Change under audit:** `pr/head.diff` — sprint-255, "guard register with origin and yield, pre-registered control arms on a record corpus, task kinds, path-scoped rule files" (81 files, 8,031 diff lines)

---

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

---

## Executive Summary

The change adds four things: a guard register generator (`guard-yield.sh`) with its origin map and floor file, a `kind:` tag rule for sprint task lines plus a release-notes ratio tool, pre-registered control arms for the eval harness (toggles in `execute-agent.sh`, the `run-arms.sh` batch driver, `arms-report.py`, the record-corpus seeder), and `paths:` scoping on two rule files. The fence hook (`block-destructive-bash.sh`) changes only by comment markers and a `replay` flag; no pattern, action or exit code moved. Secrets, injection and privacy are handled well: ids are regex-gated before they reach a path or jq, every embedded Python runs under `python3 -I`, the yield outputs carry no command, cwd or model text (probed), and the seeder fails closed when its secret scanner is missing.

The blocking defect is in the control-arm contract. The harness states that "a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never silently runs as its baseline)" (`head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:65-66`) and the README repeats it ("fails the trial (exit 2) when a toggle cannot take effect", `head/evals/README.md:509-510`). The `rule_files` toggle does not honour it, and I found two more routes to the same null experiment: a declared arm whose suite entry has no `toggles` key resolves to `{}` and runs as the baseline under its own id, and an ambient `LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES` in the operator's shell overrides every arm of a batch. Because the pre-registered verdict ("no recall loss") is documented as licence to remove a control, a null experiment is the most expensive silent failure this harness can have. Alongside: the guard-register generator can exit 0 having written nothing (reproduced), the floor leaves the fence's hook registration unprotected while the CI backstop for that gap skips on every pull request, and the new CI gates do not run for pull requests that touch only the files they guard.

What was executed, not just read: the head files were composed over a framework checkout and the new scripts and suites were run. `guard-yield.sh --hooks-table` regenerates the committed hooks table byte for byte and `--check` then reports in sync (95 guards); `guard-yield.bats` 11/11, `guard-origins.bats` 15/15, `validate-artifact-sprint-kinds.bats` 11/11, `rule-paths.bats` 6/6, `cycle-ratio.bats` 6/6, `loa-status-guards.bats` 3/3, `arm-toggles.bats` 11/11, `arms-report.bats` 7/7, `execute-agent.bats` 10/12 (EA-8/9 need `review-pr-09`, not in this change set), `recall-baseline-freshness.bats` 12/13 (BF-4 needs the committed baseline), `eval-recall-grader.bats` 26/28 (RG-16/17 need the review-prs manifests), `sprint-seams.bats` 11/12 (SEAMS-9 needs the cycle-127 fixture). `floor-snapshot.bats` skipped all four tests (no `origin/main` in the composed tree), and `run-arms.bats`, `seed-corpus.bats` and `prompt-budget.bats` need fixtures or tools outside the change set (`review-prs/pr-01`, `no-secrets.sh`, `tools/check-prompt-budget.sh`). Three defects below were reproduced directly: the generator's silent exit, the `.lock` segment and the numeric `pattern_id` abort.

**Process notes.** (1) The review gate verdict for this sprint is CHANGES_REQUIRED, not "All good"; the skill's Phase 0 would stop here. The task brief mandates an autonomous audit of the frozen PR, so the audit ran and this deviation is recorded. (2) No documentation-coherence subagent reports exist in this frozen fixture; the documentation checks below were done by hand. (3) `grimoires/loa/known-failures.md` is absent (the surface is degraded); triage ran without it.

**Security Issues Found:**

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 13 |
| Low | 22 |

---

## Critical Security Issues (Must Fix)

None.

---

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] `rule_files` control-arm toggle runs the arm as its baseline when the rules are absent

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high) — confirmed independently; the review's Changes Required §1
**File:** `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:266` (the loop at 260-267; the contract at 65-66; rule materialisation at 146)
**Issue:** The toggle removes the two rule files only if they exist, then records success either way:
```bash
for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
  if [[ -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]]; then rm -f "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r"; gone="$gone $r"; fi
  [[ ! -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]] || { echo "ERROR: rule_files toggle: $r still present" >&2; return 2; }
done
_evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"
```
Rules are copied into the sandbox only when the prompt tree has them: `if [[ -d "$PROMPT_TREE/.claude/rules" ]]` (`head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:146`). A `--source-commit` that predates the two rule files, or a tree without `.claude/rules/`, makes the toggle a no-op; the post-check at line 264 asserts absence, which is then trivially true. The other three toggles (`companion_voice` 243-247, `karpathy_block` 249-253, `audit_delta_instruction` 271-273) return 2 when they find nothing to remove. `arm-toggles.bats` AT-9 (170-179) covers that fail-closed path for them, not for `rule_files`.
**Impact:** The `no_rule_files` arm runs identically to `baseline`; `arms-report.py` reads "no recall loss"; `arm_evidence` never reaches the report. The README says the verdict may license removing a control, so a null experiment licenses deleting the two rule files. This is exactly the failure the "never silently runs as its baseline" invariant exists to prevent.
**Fix:**
```bash
[[ -n "$gone" ]] || { echo "ERROR: rule_files toggle: no rule file present in the sandbox .claude/rules/" >&2; return 2; }
_evidence rule_files "removed:$gone"
```
and add the AT-9-style case for this toggle.
**Reference:** CWE-754 Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html

---

## Medium Priority Issues

### [MED-001] A declared arm with no `toggles` key resolves to `{}` and runs as the baseline under its own id

- **File:** `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:178-186` (confidence: high)
- **Issue:** `t="$(ARM="$ARM" yq -o=json -I=0 '[.ab.arms[] | select(.id == strenv(ARM))][0].toggles // {}' "$suite_file")"` followed by `if [[ "$found" -eq 0 || -z "$t" || "$t" == "null" ]]`. A found arm whose entry lacks `toggles:` (or spells it `toggle:`) yields `found=1`, `t={}`, so `apply_toggles` loops zero times and the trial exits 0. **Issue:** The toggle removes the two rule files only if they exist, then records success either way:
```bash
for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
